task.description: Re-check (rework iteration 1) of Step 2b for ISS-0421: verify the reworked §3b/§3c/§7/§8 sections of lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md, specifically the algebraic-identity safety argument for the new Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/1 live accessor, that the accessor's shape mirrors try_acquire/2 and release/2, that no other section was disturbed, and that iteration-0's already-passed findings are not incidentally reopened.

result.summary:
New FAIL, different from iteration 0's finding, found by tracing the accessor against the ACTUAL Letflow.Admission state shape rather than the design's own narrative.

THE ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY IS SOUND IN CONCEPT BUT THE ACCESSOR AS SPECIFIED CANNOT BE BUILT FROM CURRENT STATE -- IT IS SPECIFIED AGAINST A STATE FIELD THAT DOES NOT EXIST.

Read lib/letflow/admission.ex:220-231 (init/1) directly:

```
def init(%{pool_size: pool_size, reserved_headroom: reserved_headroom}) do
  global_cap = max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1)

  {:ok,
   %{
     global_cap: global_cap,
     global_in_use: 0,
     tenants: %{},
     refs: %{}
   }}
end
```

`reserved_headroom` (like `pool_size`) is a bare `init/1` ARGUMENT consumed only to compute `global_cap`, then discarded -- it is NEVER stored anywhere in the returned state map. The state shape comment the design itself cites (admission.ex:212-219) lists exactly four keys -- `global_cap`, `global_in_use`, `tenants`, `refs` -- and `reserved_headroom` is not one of them. I independently confirmed no handle_call clause adds it either (only `global_in_use`, `tenants`, `refs` are ever mutated; `global_cap` is fixed at init and never touched again, matching the design's own claim that it's read-only post-init -- that PART of the design's premise is correct).

The design's §3b/§7 accessor spec says: 'a new handle_call(:reserved_headroom, _from, state) clause... replying with the plain integer already held in state.reserved_headroom... and leaving state unchanged... no new state field.' This is factually wrong against the code as it stands today: `state.reserved_headroom` does not exist. A GenServer built exactly to this spec would crash with a KeyError (or return nil via Map.get, if ELIXIR-DEV silently substitutes one) on the very first call to the new accessor -- every single tick, since maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 calls it fresh every invocation per this design's own §3b/§7 text.

This is not a trivial fill-in-the-blank gap for ELIXIR-DEV. Making the accessor actually work requires a REAL decision the design does not make: either (a) add `reserved_headroom` as a genuinely new field to the state map, set in init/1 alongside global_cap (which directly contradicts this same design's explicit 'no new state field' / 'purely additive to existing state, only new accessor' framing -- it's an accessor PLUS a state-shape change, not an accessor alone), or (b) have the new handle_call reconstruct reserved_headroom by re-reading Application.get_env/opts independently of what init/1 already resolved (which reopens exactly the two-independently-computed-numbers hazard this whole rework exists to close -- if start_link/1 was called with an explicit :reserved_headroom opts override, that override is baked into state.global_cap already, but recomputing it fresh from Application.get_env alone, without the opts override, would silently diverge from the value init/1 actually used for THIS instance). Neither option is stated, and the design's safety proof (global_cap + max_concurrency = pool_size, 'for any configured reserved_headroom') implicitly assumes the accessor returns the SAME reserved_headroom init/1 used for global_cap -- which is only guaranteed if option (a) is chosen and reserved_headroom is captured verbatim in state at init/1 time (not re-derived from config later, since config can change or start_link opts can differ across instances). The design does not say this, does not update the state-shape comment/doc, and explicitly claims the opposite ('no new state field').

This directly undermines the very thing this rework iteration was supposed to fix: the design still does not establish, in an implementable, checkable way, that the accessor's return value is provably the same number init/1 used to compute global_cap for that instance -- it just asserts it while citing a state shape that doesn't hold that number.

All other checks: diff between commits 1eeee5b5 and 7c4a14c8 confirmed only sections 0/3b/3c/7/8 changed -- 1, 2, 3a, 4, 5, 6 are byte-identical to the version iteration 0 already passed, so none of iteration 0's other findings (Admission arithmetic baseline, fault isolation/AC1, AC4 preservation, sequential-sweep architecture, no-literal-code) need re-verification. The accessor's calling-convention shape (defaulted `server \\ __MODULE__` argument, synchronous GenServer.call/2 delegate) does genuinely mirror try_acquire/2 (admission.ex:184-190) and release/2 (admission.ex:205-208), and is additive with respect to those two functions specifically -- that part of finding is fine, it is only the handle_call body's data source that is broken.
result.routing: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER (rework iteration 2) for lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md, §3b/§7 only. Required fix: state explicitly that Letflow.Admission's state map gains a genuinely NEW field, `reserved_headroom`, set once in init/1 from the same `reserved_headroom` argument already used to compute `global_cap` (so the two are captured from the identical value at the identical moment, per-instance) -- update the state-shape comment at admission.ex:212-219 in the design's description accordingly, and drop the 'no new state field'/'leaving state unchanged' language since it is no longer true. Then restate why this state addition, though not touching try_acquire/2 or release/2's behavior, is still additive/safe (it only adds a field nothing else reads, plus one new handle_call clause). Do not choose the config-re-read alternative (recomputing reserved_headroom from Application.get_env independently of what init/1 resolved for that instance) -- that reopens a real drift risk across differently-configured start_link/1 instances (e.g. tests) and was not evaluated as an alternative in this rework; if CODE-DESIGNER believes it is actually safe, it must justify that explicitly rather than defaulting to it. All 6 previously-passed checks and iteration 0's other findings remain passed and out of scope for this rework.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for rework iteration 2, addressing the reserved_headroom-not-in-state gap in §3b/§7 only, then re-route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-check.

gate_history.notes: Admission.global_cap arithmetic (pool_size 10 - reserved_headroom 2 = 8) independently verified correct against admission.ex/api_pipeline.ex/config. Peak-concurrency safety argument in section 3b fails: max_concurrency:2 for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 is a hardcoded literal that must stay equal to Admission's reserved_headroom for the 8+2=10 proof to hold, but nothing derives or enforces that equality -- a future independent change to reserved_headroom would silently break the pool-exhaustion safety bound. All other checks (fault isolation, AC4, sequential-sweep decision, no literal code, 2 of 3 open questions) passed.

Rework 1's live-accessor fix (Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/1) is specified to read `state.reserved_headroom`, but admission.ex's actual init/1 never stores reserved_headroom in state -- it is a bare init/1 argument consumed only to compute global_cap, then discarded; the state map holds only global_cap, global_in_use, tenants, refs. The accessor as specified would crash or require silently inventing behavior. Fixing this needs a real, undocumented state-shape change (adding reserved_headroom as a new field, captured at the same init/1 moment as global_cap) that the design explicitly denies making ('no new state field'). Diff confirmed only sections 0/3b/3c/7/8 changed; all iteration-0-passed sections (1,2,3a,4,5,6) untouched and remain passed. Accessor's calling-convention shape (defaulted server arg, GenServer.call delegate) does correctly mirror try_acquire/2 and release/2.
